correctness.rationale: Verified every inference in DRAFT.md step-by-step. Neighbor count is correct: a vertex in L={x_d=2} has exactly one neighbor in S={x_d in {0,1}} for n>=4, so needs >=d of the other 2d-1 initially infected. Failure probability P(Bin(2d-1,p)<=d-1) >= point mass C(2d-1,d-1)p^{d-1}(1-p)^d is valid. Central-binomial bound C(2d,d)>=4^d/(2 sqrt d) proved by the stated induction using (2d+1)^2>=4d(d+1) is correct; hence C(2d-1,d-1)>=4^d/(4 sqrt d). With p=(1+delta)/2, delta=2/sqrt d, the algebra p^{d-1}(1-p)^d=2^{-(2d-1)}(1-delta^2)^{d-1}(1-delta) is exact. Log bound ln(1-x)>=-x-x^2 gives (1-4/d)^{d-1}>=e^{-6} for d>=8, and 1-delta>=1/2 for d>=16, so P(F_v)>=e^{-6}/(4 sqrt d)>=e^{-8}/(4 sqrt d)=c/sqrt d holds. Packing is correct: N(v) sets for L-vertices at distance >=3 are disjoint (x_d=3 vs x_d=2 separation plus disjoint radius-1 balls), spacing-4 grid gives m=floor(n/4)^{d-1} pairwise distance >=4 for n>=8, events independent, whole-layer advance implies all succeed so probability <=(1-c/sqrt d)^m<=exp(-cm/sqrt d). Asymptotics along d(n)=floor((log log n)^3) diverge correctly. Independently recomputed exact binomial tails for d=16..400: bound holds with ratio 62-547, matching the table. Scope correctly limited to refuting the one-step mechanism, not the full window law.
